headline: Main strategy is up $3,378 on 2 of 2 winning bets, but only 18 markets have resolved, so nothing is established yet; the market price is still our best forecaster overall.
went_well: Main (Jev + Claude research) won both settled bets and is up $3,377.58. Two bets is luck-sized, not proof.
Claude direct scored a Brier of 0.097 against the market's 0.112, but it was judged on only 8 markets, possibly not the same ones.
Jev + research scored a Brier of 0.119 on 10 markets, far better than Jev alone at 0.336 on 18, so the research step looks like it matters.
went_badly: We are not beating the market: it scored 0.112 on all 18 resolved markets, and Jev + research (0.119, n=10) did not clearly beat it. In crypto (6 markets) the market scored 0.055 against research's 0.130.
Jev alone scored a Brier of 0.336 on 18 markets. That is worse than answering 50% every time (0.25), and it was worst in sports at 0.408 (n=9).

Of this week's reviewed outcomes, 2 misses were overconfidence and 2 of the 3 wins were judged lucky. The bold strategy is 1 for 3 with 25 bets still open, and the self-calibrating strategy can't start until 30 resolved markets exist (it has 10).

headline: A losing day for most strategies. Only main is ahead, at +$483 on 8 settled bets. Every Jev forecast still scores worse than the market price, and every sample here is too small to call.
went_well: Main is up $483 on 8 settled bets (4 wins, 4 losses). On the yardstick, main made +$1,173 and original +$1,136 on the same 11 bets, but only 4 have settled, so that is a tie and says nothing yet about the crypto skip.
The info gate appears to be saving money. Markets it stopped for main would have lost $44 per $100 staked (37 markets), and for Jev alone $60 per $100 (58 markets).

Claude direct's forecasts score a Brier of 0.131 (33 resolved), against 0.135 for the market price (120 resolved). The two are not scored on the same markets, so this is a hint, not proof, that Claude matches the market.
went_badly: Claude direct has lost all 4 of its settled bets, for -$8,000, despite having the best Brier score. Four bets is noise, but it suggests the gaps it bets on are its own errors rather than real edge.
Bold is down $8,545 all time (4 wins, 10 losses) and has lost all 3 bets settled since its info threshold rose to 0.35 (-$5,424). Jev alone, bold, is down $7,552 with 1 win in 6.

We are not beating the market. By Brier score, the market is at 0.135, Jev + research at 0.199 (82 resolved), Jev alone at 0.266 (120) and self-calibrating Jev at 0.236 (22). Calibration seems to make Jev worse. In economy, Jev + research scores 0.337 against the market's 0.168 (11 resolved).

went_well: Calibrated is the only strategy with a real sample that is ahead since the 30c floor (2026-10-01): 8 wins and 4 losses, +$873, about +$2.8 per $100 staked. That is 12 settled bets, so it is still an experiment, not a finding.

headline: A quiet half-day: few bets resolved, every live test is still well short of its judging point, and every forecaster except Claude on sports still scores worse than the market. So this review changes nothing and lets the running experiments collect results.
went_well: Bold, judged since its crypto skip (27 settled, 13 wins), is down only $1.6k, against $26.2k all time. That is close to the 30-settled mark, so it is still mostly noise, but it is the strategy's best stretch so far.
Jev alone, bold, judged since it stopped paying 60c and up, is +$2.7k on 11 settled (6 wins). It has 10 bets open. This is an experiment on tiny numbers, not a finding.

The favourites-only challenger (ch13) placed 7 bets in about a day after its info gate was loosened, above its 2-a-day target. Its 2 settled bets both won (+$2.2k). Claude direct is still the only forecaster that beats the market anywhere: on sports it scores 0.158 against the market's 0.175 over 14
went_badly: No forecaster beats the market overall. On the 619 markets all forecasters judged, the market scores 0.154, Claude direct 0.179, Jev + research 0.208 and Jev alone 0.249. Every non-challenger strategy is still below its $100k start.

Tuning main is not yet paying on the yardstick (the bets main and original both had the chance to place). Main is -$14.2k on 22 settled, about -$31 per $100 staked; original is -$16.3k on 32 settled, about -$21 per $100. Main has placed only 1 bet in the 1.5 days since moving to a 12c edge, on pace

Long shots still account for most of the money lost. Every strategy's all-time losses are dominated by bets under 30c: for example, main lost all 10 (-$20.5k) and bold won 2 of 25 (-$21.2k). Nothing suggests lowering the 30c floor.

The pipeline still looks broken: 48 cycles judged 0 markets, and the latest challenger (ch55) was marked invalid without a stated reason. headline: A thin half-day: the only new bets were 10 heavy-favorite wins, the Jev and Claude forecasters judged nothing for the 47th cycle running, and every strategy shown here is locked, so this review proposes no changes.
went_well: Favorites, the 'for fun' strategy, settled all 10 of its 60c-and-up bets as wins this period: +$660 on $11,972 settled, about +$5.50 per $100. That is 10 markets, so it is noise, and the review flagged 2 of the 5 wins it examined as lucky.
Mention follow is 9 wins and 4 losses, +$191 on $584 staked, about +$33 per $100. That rests on only 13 settled bets, and its forecaster's measured edge over the price is still 0 on 36 markets.
Claude direct is still the only forecaster that beats the market anywhere with real numbers behind it: in sports it scores a Brier of 0.177 against the market's 0.181 on 203 markets.
went_badly: None of our own forecasters beats the market overall. On 849 markets they all scored, the market's Brier is 0.164, Claude direct's 0.201 and Jev + research's 0.217 (lower is better). Nothing new was judged in 47 cycles, and main, original, bold, calibrated and the challengers are still missing from

Mention NO is 19 wins and 37 losses on 56 settled, -$234 on $2,481 staked, about -$9 per $100. Its forecaster nonetheless now shows a positive measured edge (lambda 0.09 on 815 markets), and its win and loss counts still don't reconcile with its P&L (p48, p51).

Favorites has 40 bets still open out of $55.6k staked in total, so roughly $43k, about 44% of its bankroll, rides on unresolved markets. Sharp has lost both of its bets (-$499), and its live minimum edge still reads 3c although the change to 2c (p33) is marked applied (p36, p44).

headline: A quiet half day: Jev and Claude forecast nothing for the 18th review running, so only the four locked strategies bet. Their totals are too thin to call, and none can be tuned.
went_well: Favorites is 15 for 15 on settled heavy-favorite bets, +$964 on $17.0k settled stake (about +$5.70 per $100). That is the small, steady return you'd expect at 60c and up. It rests on 15 bets, so it is not yet a finding.
Mention follow is 9 wins and 4 losses, +$191 on about $443 settled stake (about +$43 per $100). That is only 13 settled markets, so it is mostly noise.

Claude direct still edges the market in sports (Brier 0.177 vs 0.181 on 203 markets) and culture (0.032 vs 0.074, only 14 markets). It is the only forecaster beating the price anywhere, and only narrowly.
went_badly: None of the 48 cycles judged a single market, so main, original, calibrated and the Claude strategies are still missing. No Jev- or Claude-driven strategy can bet, be measured or be tuned. Overall, the market price (Brier 0.163 paired, 851 markets) still beats every forecaster: Claude 0.201, Jev + r

Mention NO is 19 wins and 37 losses on 56 settled, -$234 on about $1.7k settled stake (about -$13 per $100). Its NO bets at 30-60c won 13 of 43 (30%), and at 60c+ only 6 of 13 (46%), both below what the prices implied. Yet its skill estimate is positive (lambda 0.13 on 848 markets), and the two disa

Sharp lost both its bets (-$499, 2 settled). Its live rules still show min_edge 0.03 at version 1, although p33 (2c) is marked applied, and its gate ledger counts 1 bet where its record shows 2. strategies.name: mention_follow
strategies.label: Mention markets, follow the first NO

recent_rule_changes.why: In crypto, Jev + research scores 0.151 against the market's 0.087 over 56 resolved markets. Bold is down $20.3k, the worst of any strategy, on 33 settled. Skipping crypto leaves bold differing from main only in its info gate (0.35 vs 0.5), which makes it a clean test of that gate.
recent_rule_changes.judge_by: On bets opened after this change, bold's P&L per $100 staked beats its current all-time -$22 per $100, and is within $10 per $100 of main's over the same period.

recent_rule_changes.why: Claude direct's forecasts trail the market (paired Brier 0.182 vs 0.153 on 357 markets), so its 8c 'edges' are probably mostly error. Its bets lose $68 per $100 (9 settled). This is an experiment; ch3 tried a pickier Claude direct and was retired, but it did that without the 30c floor.
recent_rule_changes.judge_by: On bets opened after this change, P&L per $100 staked beats claude_direct's all-time -$51 per $100 and is no worse than main's over the same period.

recent_rule_changes.why: Jev alone, bold has lost all 3 of its bets at 60c and up (-$6.0k), while its 30-60c bets are +$914 on 6. Jev alone is the weakest forecaster (Brier 0.235), and paying 60c+ leaves little room for its error. This rests on only 3 bets, so it is an experiment.
recent_rule_changes.judge_by: On bets opened after this change, P&L per $100 staked beats its since-floor -$4.9 per $100 and its all-time -$43 per $100.

recent_rule_changes.why: Sports is the only category where any forecaster beats the market (Claude 0.158 vs market 0.176, on 131 markets), yet ch16 has placed 1 bet in about 2.5 days. The 4 markets stopped only by Jev's info gate would have paid +$77 per $100. Jev's own information rating may say little about Claude's forecast. This is an experiment on tiny numbers.
recent_rule_changes.judge_by: On bets opened after this change, ch16's P&L per $100 staked is positive and ahead of claude_direct's over the same period.

recent_rule_changes.why: Jev + research trails the market by about 0.06 Brier on 559 paired markets, so many of its 8c 'edges' are probably forecast error. Main loses about $26 per $100 since the floor (11 settled) and trails original per dollar on the yardstick (-$32 vs -$22 per $100). Requiring 12c, as claude_direct now does, tests whether fewer, stronger-conviction bets lose less. This is an experiment on small numbers.
recent_rule_changes.judge_by: On bets opened after this change, main's P&L per $100 staked on the yardstick (shared markets) is better than original's over the same period, and better than main's since-floor -$26 per $100. If main places fewer than 10 bets in a week, revert to 0.08.

recent_rule_changes.why: ch13 has placed only 5 bets in about 4.5 days. The 30 markets it skipped only because of Jev's info gate would have returned +$4.15 per $100 (19 wins), the only gate-blocked group in the ledger with a meaningful count that shows a profit. Lowering the gate from 0.5 to 0.35, bold's setting, should give it more bets at 55c and up. This is an experiment on noisy numbers.
recent_rule_changes.judge_by: On bets opened after this change, ch13 places at least 2 bets a day, and its P&L per $100 staked is positive and no worse than calibrated's over the same period.

recent_rule_changes.why: Claude trails the market badly outside sports: politics 0.255 vs 0.117 (13 markets), weather 0.208 vs 0.072 (19), other 0.138 vs 0.099 (19), crypto 0.134 vs 0.110 (37). It beats the market in sports (0.161 vs 0.177, 146 markets) and probably in culture (0.040 vs 0.089, but only 5 markets). Since its edge rose to 12c it has settled only 2 bets, so this is an experiment. It also sets up a comparison with ch16: a strict sports Claude (12c edge, info gate 0.5) against a loose one (8c edge, info gate 0.2).
recent_rule_changes.judge_by: On bets opened after this change, Claude direct's P&L per $100 staked is positive and beats its all-time -$55 per $100. We also compare it with ch16's over the same period to see whether the strict or the loose sports setup earns more per $100.

recent_rule_changes.why: Jev + research trails the market most in crypto (0.168 vs 0.104 on 152 markets), politics (0.260 vs 0.117 on 45) and economy (0.232 vs 0.103 on 42). Main and bold already skip crypto, but calibrated, the best-performing Jev strategy (-$2.7k on 17 settled since the price floor), does not.
recent_rule_changes.judge_by: On bets opened after this change, calibrated's settled P&L per $100 staked beats its since-floor figure of about -$6 per $100. That figure includes open stake, so it is approximate. It should also be no worse than main's over the same period.

recent_rule_changes.why: Jev + research trails the market least in sports (0.205 vs 0.178 on 539 markets) and far more elsewhere: politics 0.260 vs 0.117, economy 0.232 vs 0.103, other 0.232 vs 0.103, weather 0.219 vs 0.085. Bold's info-gate test has told us little: markets stopped only by that gate lose about the same as bets placed (-$31 vs -$31 per $100 on 167 and 62), so bold's slot is better spent testing whether Jev + research can earn in its best category. This is an experiment.
recent_rule_changes.judge_by: On bets opened after this change, bold's settled P&L per $100 staked beats its v4 figure of about -$9 per $100 and beats main's over the same period. If bold places fewer than 1 bet a day, restore its previous categories.

recent_rule_changes.why: Sharp has placed 1 bet ever under a 3c-after-fees edge requirement, so we are learning nothing about whether Pinnacle's line beats these prices. A de-vigged sharp line is a strong forecaster, and a 2c edge is a reasonable experiment while sizing is probe-only anyway. If the real cause is a matching or data bug (p30), this change will do nothing, and that itself tells us something.
recent_rule_changes.judge_by: Within 3 days sharp places at least 1 bet a day. If it doesn't, the bottleneck is coverage, not the edge requirement, and this should be reverted. After enough settle, its settled P&L per $100 staked is zero or better.

went_well: Favorites is 18 for 18 (+$1,087 on $19.3k settled, about +$5.6 per $100). That is still under 30 results, and it is bets at 60c and up winning as favorites usually do. It is not evidence of edge.
Mention follow is 9 wins and 4 losses, +$191 on $647 staked (about +$29 per $100). Its 4 bets at 60c and up all won. This rests on 13 settled markets, so it is noise until it passes 30.
One of the 2 markets reviewed this period was a win credited to research finding the answer.
went_badly: No forecaster judged a single market in 48 cycles, and main, original, calibrated, bold and claude_direct are absent again, along with the yardstick.
